description: We are Future Entrepreneurs, a team of ambitious students passionate about space exploration, science, and technology. Our goal is to combine creativity, research, and innovation to develop solutions to real-world challenges. We believe in teamwork, fresh perspectives, and thinking outside the box. We may be young, but we're curious, motivated, and ready to turn big ideas into reality!
summary: "Orbital Health" is a digital health-monitoring application designed to support astronauts during long-duration space missions. We developed an interactive web-based prototype that brings important health information together in one place. It includes five main features: Health Dashboard, Daily Check-in, Health Trends, Smart Alerts, and Health History. The application allows astronauts to record daily health indicators, track changes over time, and identify unusual patterns by comparing new measurements with their personal baseline. Orbital Health addresses the challenges of monitoring physical and mental well-being in space, where microgravity, isolation, sleep disturbances, and limited access to medical facilities can affect astronauts' health. Our project aims to make health information easier to understand, encourage regular monitoring, and support communication about potential health concerns. We believe that better health awareness can contribute to safer and more successful space missions. "Orbital Health – Your Health, Beyond Earth."
details: Orbital Health is a digital health-monitoring application designed to support astronauts during long-duration space missions. Its main purpose is to make health information easier to collect, understand, and monitor in the challenging environment of space. The application works through five main features. The Health Dashboard displays the astronaut's latest health information, while Daily Check-in allows users to enter measurements such as heart rate, sleep duration, fatigue, and mood. Health Trends presents changes over time through charts. Smart Alerts identifies unusual changes by comparing new measurements with the astronaut's personal baseline and provides an explanation and a suggested next step. Finally, Health History stores previous records for easy access. The main benefits of Orbital Health are better organization of health information, easier tracking of individual changes, and increased awareness of potential health concerns. Our intended impact is to support astronauts in monitoring their physical and mental well-being and contribute to safer, better-informed space missions. We developed a web-based interactive prototype using AI-assisted development tools. The application includes a responsive interface, interactive elements, health indicators, and data visualizations. We use clearly labeled simulated data to demonstrate its functionality. What makes our project creative is its focus on personal health baselines. Instead of treating all astronauts the same, the application compares each user's measurements with their own usual patterns. This allows for a more individual approach to health monitoring. During development, our team considered the unique challenges of space exploration, including microgravity, isolation, sleep disturbances, limited access to medical facilities, and the importance of a simple and accessible interface. Orbital Health is designed as a prototype and does not provide medical diagnoses or replace professional medical care. It demonstrates how digital technology can support astronaut health monitoring and has potential for further development and integration with real health-monitoring devices.
